messages:
Jordan (oncall_sre): Heads up — us-midwest1 egress interfaces are flapping with provider AS64512. We're seeing packet loss to internal S3 endpoints, model loads failing, and the GPU pool moved into degraded state. Rolling traffic off the affected AZ now.

Pat (networking): Confirmed the provider pushed unstable BGP updates at 14:03:21 UTC. AS path churn is causing route instability. I'm on the provider bridge, working with them. Estimated stabilization 15–30m unless they roll back.

Priya (eng-infra): Observed node churn: ~40% of gpu-pool-umw1 reporting storage timeouts -> loader failures. Autoscaler has paused new allocations to avoid noisy retries. Can we shift customer traffic to us-east2 and eu-west1 for prod?

Marta (support_lead): Support: preparing customer notifications for affected Dedicated tenants in umw1. Need ETA and confirmation of failover plan. @Priya can you confirm the regions + risks (latency/cost)?

Priya (eng-infra): Confirming — I'll initiate a controlled traffic-shift for hostgroups tagged 'prod' to us-east2 first, then eu-west1 if needed. Note: cross-region egress will increase token latency and egress costs. Dry-run looks good, executing now.

SupportBot: /incident create incident-2025-umw1-egress severity:high notify:pager+statuspage

Jordan (oncall_sre): Action list: 1) Apply NLB reroute to avoid affected AZ 2) Drain affected GPU nodes 3) Force autoscaler resume once nodes drained 4) Post status update. Doing step 1 now.

Pat (networking): Provider says they rolled a temporary more-specific but flaps resumed after ~8 mins. They're escalating internally; gave a soft ETA of 30m unless stable.

Alex (cost-ops): Heads up — cross-region shift will materially increase egress charges for some tenants (esp those with large embedding workloads). Ballpark +$8k–$15k/day if the shift persists. Recommend flagging cost-sensitive customers in the notice.

Marta (support_lead): Draft statuspage copy: "Investigating increased errors and timeouts in us-midwest1 impacting model loads. We are shifting traffic to alternate regions; some customers may see degraded throughput or increased latency. Engineers are working with the network provider. ETA: 30–60 minutes." Approve? :thinking_face:

Priya (eng-infra): Approve. Adding note about temporary throttling for very large requests while caches warm. Also posting the command used for audit:```bash
./shift-traffic --from=us-midwest1 --to=us-east2 --tag=prod --dry-run=false
```

Jordan (oncall_sre): Update @channel: traffic shift completed for prod hostgroups at 14:10 UTC. Error rate dropped from ~7% -> ~1.2%. KV cache warming will cause a small spike in tail latency for ~10–20m. Leaving incident open until provider confirms BGP stability and we see 30m of clean routing. :thumbsup:

Marta (support_lead): Notifying impacted customers with the approved copy and cost note. Escalations: none yet. Will update if any enterprise accounts open support tickets.

Pat (networking): Provider just pushed a clean route set at 14:22 UTC and reports no further flaps in the last 2m. Continuing to monitor.

Jordan (oncall_sre): Closing loop: keep this thread for postmortem notes. We'll capture timeline + cost impact and propose mitigations (eg reduce inter-region egress during failover, add extra route dampening with provider)"
